reviews.title: Great App! No Customer Service.
reviews.text: Great app and super motivating! I would give it a 5 out of 5 review if it was not for the customer service. Six attempts to reach Shred over 2 weeks about a glitch in the software. I did all usually fixes - log out/in, hard stop, power off/on, removed app, etc. Only responses are automated responses saying they will respond in 24-48 hours. Zero customer support!!!

reviews.title: Best fitness app
reviews.text: I’ve tried several other fitness apps, shred is proven to me. I lost about 15lbs in a year and gained clear muscle tone and stamina. The app works perfectly with my home gym and the videos help to make sure you’re doing the workout properly. I use it, my kids use it and I’ve turned some friends on to it as well. Get this app and you’ll see results!

reviews.title: Terrible CS
reviews.text: I’ve reached out via email and their support over 8 times with an app timeout/break issue. Never a single reply. So 2 stars.

reviews.title: Needs Another Update
reviews.text: App is great overall. New exercises and routines that pushed me in new directions, and most importantly, left me sore and seeing results. The bad: app needs updating. It doesn't always sync between apple watch and app so when you cycle through an exercise on the watch, it sometimes skips entire exercises and sets. You have to hit back and it assumes you want to repeat an exercise. Also, wish there was a program to hit legs and arms twice a week. It seems to cycle through body parts so even if you ask for a 5 day weekly workout, next sessions is a new region like shoulders or back, so only really get to upper or lower in total once a week, maybe 1.5 since there are focused next sessions. But not ideal and wish there were more options

reviews.title: Degraded Quality
reviews.text:
Have been using this app for about 5 months and have enjoyed it, but the quality has gone down and they’re not improving features quickly enough. The AI coach voice that gives instructions has gotten weird in the last few weeks, sounding robotic and sometimes British (not the coach I have selected). 

Also, we’ve been asking for muscle group heatmaps for months and they’re not delivering. 

I emails support about the voice issue and haven’t heard back. Can’t recommend this app anymore and considering changing.

reviews.title: Somewhat questionable
reviews.text: Started out really liking this app but I don’t like the limitations on modifying your workouts after you start a particular workout. Can’t add sets or new workouts, and even alternates seem like they’re limited. They also don’t have basic exercises like adductor machines. Also finding it highly suspicious that they no longer show the 1st place person anymore so you have no idea how close you are to being first. Seems like you should also be able to interact with other users more than just a cheer. I also find myself having to modify workouts more often than not because it’ll have me doing every single variation of a particular move (I.e bent over row underhand, then overhand. Then dumbbell then machine. Like wtf)

reviews.title: Missing feature in recent updates
reviews.text: Why does it no longer show the user in first place (gold) and load during workouts anymore?  Seems like an odd way to represent the challenge…

reviews.title: Repetitive, Redundant Programming
reviews.text:
I subscribed to SHRED because I wanted structured, balanced programming without having to design and correct every workout myself. Unfortunately, the app regularly stacks minor variations of essentially the same exercise within one session.

My latest leg workout prescribed four rounds of barbell sumo squats, followed by three rounds of sumo deadlifts, and then three rounds of dumbbell sumo squats. The previous workout included dumbbell curls, rope cable curls, and combination curls—all in the same session.

I understand that the same muscle can benefit from complementary exercises, but these movements overlap so heavily that the programming feels padded rather than purposeful. The combination curl even repeats much of what the other two curl variations already accomplish.

The interface and demonstrations are polished, but I should not have to audit and replace multiple exercises when personalized programming is the feature I’m paying for. Until the workout construction becomes more thoughtful, balanced, and consistent, I cannot recommend the paid subscription.

reviews.title: Great Workouts Clunky App
reviews.text:
The workouts themselves are excellent. The videos of each exercise are really helpful. The app itself is pretty clunky and unintuitive.

For my two cents:

I want to be able to see my calendar of the next weeks workouts while I’m in the middle of one. But to do that you have to quit your current workout.

 I want to be able to start one exercise in a circuit and be able to switch mid circuit, not have to skip a few. 

I want to know what weights I’ll need for the current circuit at the beginning. Not have to find out at each exercise. 

I want clearer indications of when a pyramid set or 

I want clearer indications of when to go up weight/down weight in my circuit. 

I want to be able to see the timer while looking at the next exercise. 

In a circuit, I’m much more likely to do fewer reps or more reps than go up/down a weight, so I want it to default to changing reps, not weight. There should be  + - buttons on the exercise itself, not another modal that opens. And I don’t want to always use the keypad. 

If I hit exhaustion on a muscle group, I want to be able to record that more easily.

reviews.title: Not gonna resubscribe
reviews.text: This app got me started and that’s awesome but I’ve discovered so many problems. Ask AI about this app before putting money down. This app will not push data for some workouts or it will do it hours later with wrong data like it never ended the workout. Maybe because I hit end workout then when I go back in later to download my pic the end button is there like I never it hit. What’s my PR for bench press? I don’t know and the app doesn’t keep track for PR for the user. It will tell you when you hit a PR but you can’t go back and look at your PR’s. Often I get instructions in English follows by instructions in random unrecognizable Slavic sounding languages. If I tap the video the text doesn’t go away anymore forcing me to go into full screen mode. Doesn’t always show enough angles. I’m often wondering where my hands are supposed to be. There is no settings or ability to enlarge text even though theres plenty of blank space. Whatever next year I’m trying Fitbod

reviews.title: Motivating but needs customization
reviews.text:
I feel Shred is one of the most motivating fitness apps I’ve used and I’ve used them all. It has just enough of the community element without being distracting or influencer driven. The workouts are challenging and you can customize based on frequency and equipment.

So why four stars? For anyone who’s mildly experience with training or weight lifting, you’ll find yourself wishing for more control over workouts. For example, I can’t create my own from-scratch workout. You have to rely on what Shred’s algorithm creates for you. Also, for workouts skew MUCH longer. A “30 minute” workout usually lasts me
45 mins to an 60 mins or more, and I follow the rests accurately. 

Also, if you really like data about your progress, this app may not be for you. It’s impossible to find PRs for individual exercises unless you’re in the middle of a workout (there’s a button to see historical data for an exercise there).

Another quirk with Shred is editing. Sometimes i like to edit my days workout in advance. But, if you close the app, it loses your edits and you have to start all over.

Overall, Shred is outstanding and motivating despite some quirks.

reviews.title: Membership Cancelled - glitchy and useless ai
reviews.text:
I’ve been using the app for almost a year now and over the past few months it has become extremely glitchy

The ai does not make adjustments to workouts despite that being advertised, i think I’ve told it over 5 times over the past few months to give me more machine oriented workouts (yes the relevant equipment is selected in settings) and it just doesn’t listen despite giving a confirmation “the next workout will include more machine oriented workouts”

The phone app and apple watch app lose sync causing incorrect data being written to apple health

The apps buttons just stop working during workouts, clicking next before a rest doesn’t go to rest but the next workout begins. Force quitting restores functionality but I’ve had a workout completely reset as a result OR the app recovers but the apple watch app thinks you have the workout paused

Not sure if the devs have embraced vibe coding recently, but recent app performance tells me “probably”

Canceling membership and going back to traditional workout tracking, really wanted this app to work out!

reviews.title: Phenomenal App
reviews.text:
Whether I’m working out on the go or at my home gym, this app can do it all. Though the company has true fitness gurus, it also has a strong continuous improvement mindset which has shown app improvements on a regular basis. Any company can scam you one time, but a great company makes you want to do business with them year after year. 
I appreciate the tailored workouts and interactions where you are cheered on by the global community! It has helped me to remain focused and committed in ways other apps (and in person gyms) did not. Excited to see what’s next from this app!

reviews.title: My Personal Trainer—No Matter Where I Am
reviews.text:
I’ve been using Shred since the beginning, and it continues to get better every year. As an athlete who travels frequently, consistency in training is critical, and Shred makes that easy.

The app provides structured, effective workouts wherever I am, eliminating the need to constantly create new programs or figure out what to do in the gym. Whether I’m training at home, traveling for competition, or working out in a hotel gym, I always have a plan that keeps me on track.

For me, Shred is like having a personal trainer in my pocket—an essential tool for maintaining fitness, performance, and accountability no matter where life takes me.

reviews.title: Great App!!
reviews.text: The exercises are an excellent collection of different angles to hit the target muscles. I love the layout and the AI interaction. I also love how the app announces your next exercises and the last weight you used. This is fantastic for setting up without having to look at my phone. I do have a complaint about the inability to adjust the voice volume in conjunction to the volume of my music. I have to raise my volume to hear the trainers voice then back down because it results in my music being too loud. Very annoying. It defeats the purpose of not interfacing with my phone between circuits.. The other complaint I have is the font size is too small and I sometimes have to reach for reading glasses. Not great when you’re trying to keep a pace.. These seem to be easy fixes that I’d like to see implemented.  These two issues keep me from using the app. I use Fitbod when I’m not feeling up to dealing with these issues, but I would Shred exclusively if they were fixed because I love the exercise combinations.

reviews.title: Why so complicated
reviews.text: I just want to workout and be healthy. The gym isn’t a “lifestyle”. I have a life. I just want to go to the gym to stay healthy and have an app help me. This thing requires all your info, exactly what weights and machines are at your gym. Min 3 days per week. What if I start with 1? Does that make me a bad person and shouldn’t use the app?!? Why can’t I just say. I’m looking for a general all around workout schedule. When I come back next is my next workout regardless of the days in between. I don’t want daily notifications and a constant email. I’m not looking to join a community. I just want to be a little healthier than I am now. Why is that so hard for you fanatics to understand!!
